title: Older CFC-12 and SF6 ages account for 53-67% of the AOU increase on sigma0 26.5 on three of four North Atlantic and North Pacific repeat sections, but for only 26% on P16N
abstract: Question: on the sigma0 = 26.5 kg/m3 surface, is the oxygen loss found at CalCOFI and BATS a ventilation change or an AOU change at fixed water age? Approach: we used GLODAPv2.2023 bottle data from repeat sections A22 (passes BATS) and A20 (1997, 2003, 2012, 2021), P02 east of 160 W (1994, 2004, 2013; ends at the CalCOFI grid), P16N (1991, 2006, 2015) and P03 east (1985, 2005). We calculated inverse-Gaussian transit-time-distribution ages from CFC-12 and SF6, with a width ratio that makes the two tracer ages agree (1.15-1.5). We compared paired along-track bins and moved each early value along the early AOU-age relation by the age change (ventilation part V). Results: from the first to the last occupation, AOU increased by 18-24 umol/kg on all four main sections. The tracer age increased by 3.7-10.7 years. V explained 66% of the AOU increase on A22 (12.7 of 19.2 umol/kg), 53% on A20, 67% on P02 east and 26% on P16N. A positive AOU increase at fixed age (6.5-17.1 umol/kg) remained on every section. On A22, AOU and age changed in the same direction in all three intervals. On P02 east, AOU rose by 21.6 umol/kg in 1994-2004 with a small age change (V 4.7), and age rose in 2004-2013 with little AOU change. This AOU timing matches CalCOFI, but the age timing does not. Limitations: the results depend on the TTD model and on inter-cruise tracer calibration, which GLODAP does not adjust; one crossover shows a CFC-12 disagreement of about 7 years. Intervals do not include calibration error. Sections are near or upstream of the time-series sites. We did not test climate models.
